mappings.note: Gap-fill on the Doctor's reaction, answered by choosing between 'certainty/curiosity' and 'write/memorise' from what the text says. Comprehension of a text, so LO-1; LO-10 was rejected because the choice is semantic, not grammatical. Stem is corrupted -- the tail of the previous answer ('knows more about animals than the local veterinarians.') is prepended.

Speculates about challenges Dolittle would face if more animals came, and how he would solve them. Entirely outside the text, which is CG-ENG2's 'go beyond the text'; no LO covers hypothetical extension. Stem is corrupted -- it opens with the stray answer 'Farm animals wearing glasses.'
'How can we say that Polynesia was a good trainer' -- the text never calls her one; the reader must judge from her behaviour. CG-ENG2 branch (LO-7), not the retrieval LO.
How he gave each animal individual attention. The text narrates the listening and treating, so this is retrieval assembled into a paragraph.
Asks what his willingness to follow the parrot shows about listening to other viewpoints -- a generalisation the text never makes. CG-ENG2 branch.
Name the qualities that made him famous and support them from the text. The traits must be inferred from incidents, so LO-7 rather than LO-1.
What would change if everyone could talk to animals -- a hypothetical about the real world. Goal level; no LO covers it.

Pre-reading prompt about the student's own pet, explicitly to be shared with classmates and the teacher. LO-4 (conversations with friends and others) rather than LO-3, which is for staged forms like debate, skit or speech. Stored answer is truncated by the pdf.tube footer and opens like a speech.
Extract with four sub-questions: three are answerable from the lines (LO-1), while (i) asks which exclamation could replace 'Good Gracious' -- a vocabulary/register item, hence LO-9 as well.

Extract (the plough horse's green glasses) with an analogy to be completed from a word in the passage and a word for the Doctor's attitude. Both are anchored in the printed lines, so retrieval. (NODIA watermark in the answer.)

'Let us listen' task: hear an announcement and mark a statement true or false. Listening comprehension has no LO of its own -- LO-1 and LO-2 cover texts and instructions -- so the listening goal is cited. Stem is corrupted: the answer key of a present-perfect grammar exercise ('has learnt, 2. has treated...') is prepended.

'Let us speak': take turns playing doctor and patient using cue cards. That is role play, which LO-3 names; LO-4 was rejected because the roles and content are scripted rather than a free conversation. Stem is corrupted -- the answer key of the preceding listening gap-fill ('Woodstock, 2. Rose, 3. 9...') is prepended.

Badly truncated stem: one option of a list about caring for stray animals ('Adopt them by taking them home') plus 'Give reasons for your responses.' The recoverable task is a reasoned personal opinion, which only the goal statement covers -- it is not a question on a text (LO-1) and no LO covers opinion-giving.
MCQ on what kind of doctor he was at first. Stated fact. Retrieval.
MCQ, who first suggested the change (the Cat's-food-Man). Stated. Retrieval. (pdf.tube footer in the answer.)
MCQ on the ability he learnt (animal language). Stated. Retrieval.
MCQ on the horse's reason for wanting glasses -- quoted in the extract. Retrieval.
MCQ on how animals talk besides with their mouths. Quoted list. Retrieval.
MCQ on what Theodosia did with the book (read it aloud). Stated detail.
MCQ naming the dog (Jip). Stated detail.
MCQ on what the old ladies brought. Stated detail.
MCQ on where Polynesia sat. Stated detail.
MCQ on what the dog's twitching nose meant -- Polynesia translates it in the text. Retrieval, not inference.
MCQ on how animals abroad heard of him (migrating birds). Stated. Retrieval. (NODIA watermark.)
MCQ on what he was doing at the moment Polynesia suggested it. Stated detail.
MCQ on why the flowerpots went outside (for rainwater). Stated. Retrieval. Minor defect: option (A) reads 'To watered them'.
MCQ on Polynesia's two languages. Stated. Retrieval.
MCQ on the cat's-food-man's remark about a past life. Quoted joke, retrieval.
MCQ on Polynesia's verdict on other animal doctors. Quoted opinion, retrieval.
MCQ on the outcome of learning animal languages. Stated. Retrieval.
MCQ on how he felt about his new life. The text says he was happy. Retrieval.
MCQ on the horse's view of what a good animal doctor takes. Quoted line. Retrieval.
How the Cat's-food-Man convinced him -- his two arguments are on the page. Retrieval.
Explain Polynesia's use of two languages, with the quoted examples. Retrieval.
His reaction and immediate action (fetching book and pencil). Both narrated. Retrieval.
How animals communicate without their mouths, 'according to Polynesia'. Quoted. Retrieval.
Why he gave up human patients. The text gives the reason. Retrieval.
The horse's eye problem and its request. Both quoted. Retrieval.
What became a common sight around Puddleby. Stated. Retrieval.
How speaking animal languages made treatment easier -- the text says the animals told him where the pain was. Retrieval.
The special doors and their labels. Listed in the text. Retrieval.
How his fame spread. Stated (cured animals and migrating birds). Retrieval.
How he manages the crowds of animals -- the labelled doors and tunnels are described in the text. Retrieval. (NODIA watermark.)
Assertion-Reason on the Cat's-food-Man's motive; the student must decide whether R explains A. Reasoning about the text, so LO-7, unlike the recall MCQs around it.
Assertion-Reason linking the crowded garden to the animals' discovery. Causal judgement, LO-7.
One-line recall of who suggested the change. Retrieval.
Which book Theodosia read. Stated. Retrieval.
How many languages Polynesia speaks. Stated number. Retrieval.
The meaning of 'Ka-ka oi-ee, fee-fee?'. The text translates it, so this is retrieval rather than a vocabulary item (LO-9 was rejected for that reason).
How animals 'speak' besides with their mouths. Quoted. Retrieval.
What the plough horse needed instead of pills (spectacles). Stated. Retrieval.
The common sight around Puddleby, in one line. Retrieval.
What animals told him once he understood them. Quoted. Retrieval.
What was written over the front door ('HORSES'). Stated. Retrieval.
How he became world famous, in one line. Retrieval. (NODIA watermark.)
Assertion-Reason where R (high fees) is invented and must be tested against the text. Reasoning, LO-7.
Assertion-Reason where R contradicts Polynesia's explanation about animals talking with ears, feet and tails. Testing a claim, LO-7.
Assertion-Reason on the special doors and the waiting mice. Explanatory fit, LO-7.
Why the Cat's-food-Man makes his suggestion -- his reasons are in the dialogue. Retrieval in extended form.
How Polynesia teaches him animal languages -- the rainy-afternoon lesson is narrated. Retrieval.
